## project.close

Closes the open project; the editor shows its launcher. Without a project it does nothing. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the project file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save), unless force is true (save first). Waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first, also with force: a save is never lost. Returns closed, discardedChanges and discardedSettings (whether unsaved scene changes or unwritten settings were discarded).

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `assets` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorAssetCommands.cpp:346`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | boolean | no |   | Go on although the edited scene has unsaved changes, discarding them (default false: the command fails instead). Discarded changes are kept as recovery data of the project (scene.recoveryStatus), and the person at the editor is told who discarded them. |

## project.create

Creates a project in a directory and opens it. With template &quot;basic3d&quot; it starts with a saved, lit start scene (Scenes/Main.stscene: Main Camera, Sun, Sky, Ground, Post Process); the default &quot;empty&quot; has no scene (see project.templates). Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save), unless force is true (save first), before anything is created; waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first. Returns projectFile, template, startScene, discardedChanges and discardedSettings (whether unsaved scene changes or unwritten settings were discarded).

| `name` | string | yes |   | Project name. |
| `template` | string | no |   | What the project starts with (default &quot;empty&quot;; see project.templates). One of: `empty`, `basic3d`. |

## project.export

Exports the project as a playable game (runtime executable, asset pack, script module, manifest) into a directory outside the project, in the background: the editor keeps running, and the command answers when the export finished (it fails at once when it cannot start, and fails naming the document when a scene, prefab or material saved meanwhile references what the export did not plan for: export again, or when the save of the scene in flight that it started during fails). The pack is ordered by first use from the start scene; with prune it holds only what the scenes use and what the project's Export.AlwaysInclude names (project.setExportSettings), and excludedAssets lists what it left out. The game runs the script module the editor has loaded (build it first with script.build). The manifest carries the game's identity (project.setGameInfo: the title its window shows, version, company, copyright) and, with an icon, icon names &lt;File&gt;.png next to it, 256 x 256 pixels, made from the icon's image (it fails when that does not decode). On Linux hosts a game with the runtime gets &lt;File&gt;.desktop too, a desktop entry naming the export's absolute paths. Returns the files (icon and desktopEntry: null without one), assetCount, the pack's size, seconds, warnings (an enlarged icon, a desktop entry left out) and frameTimes (the editor's frames from the one that started the export to its end, like editor.wait's).

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `assets` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorAssetCommands.cpp:457`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cookDocuments` | boolean | no |   | Put scenes, prefabs and models into the pack in their binary cooked form, which loads without parsing JSON (default true; false keeps their JSON). |
| `directory` | string | yes |   | Absolute output directory outside the project (created when missing). |
| `fullscreen` | boolean | no |   | Start in fullscreen (default false). |
| `height` | integer | no |   | Window height (default 720). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |
| `includeRuntime` | boolean | no |   | Copy the runtime executable (default true). |
| `includeScriptSymbols` | boolean | no |   | Copy the script module's debug symbols (PDB) too (default: true, false in Dist builds). |
| `prune` | boolean | no |   | Leave out assets no scene uses and Export.AlwaysInclude does not name (default false: scripts may load assets by path). |
| `runtime` | string | no |   | Runtime executable to copy (default: StrataRuntime next to the editor). |
| `width` | integer | no |   | Window width (default 1280). Value: at least `1`, at most `16384`. |

## project.open

Opens a project file or the project in a directory. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save), unless force is true (save first); waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first, also with force. The project opens at once; its start scene loads in the background like scene.open's (the frames go on, scene.loadStatus reports it) and the command answers once it is the edited scene: {projectFile, discardedChanges and discardedSettings (whether unsaved scene changes or unwritten settings were discarded), settingsProblems (\[{section, message}\]: settings sections whose stored values are refused, kept as stored while their defaults apply; set or reset them with project.setSettings), startScene (null when the project has none), startSceneOpened, startSceneError (why it was not opened; the project stays open with an empty scene), seconds (the start scene's load), migrated (null, or for a project saved by 0.5.0 or older, which is migrated once before its start scene opens and written as the current version: {collisionLayers: {scenes: those whose layers became the project's, conflicts, unreadable}})}.

## project.openSample

Copies a sample project (project.samples) into a new directory and opens the copy, like project.open; the sample itself stays unchanged. The copy leaves out local editor data (.strata): build its scripts with script.build before playing. Fails while the edited scene has unsaved changes, or the open project's file unwritten settings, unless force is true (save first), before anything is copied; waits for saves in flight (scene.save, the project file) first. It answers once the start scene is open, with project.open's fields (projectFile, discardedChanges, discardedSettings, settingsProblems, the start scene's) and sample.

## project.setCollisionLayers

Names the project's collision layers and sets which of them collide, as one undo step that leaves the scene saved, and writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it). The layers are the project's: every scene and prefab uses the same 32 layers, names and matrix (scene.info's settings.physicsLayers shows them as the active scene runs them). layerNames apply first, then resetLayerCollisions, then layerCollisions in order; an invalid request changes nothing. Allowed while playing: the running game takes the new table at once (replacing what its scripts changed with Physics:\:SetLayersCollide) and the change stays after play.stop. Returns physicsLayers ({names, noCollisions}, pairs by name).

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `settings` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorProjectSettingsCommands.cpp:323`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layerCollisions` | array of object | no |   | Changes of the layer matrix, applied in order after layerNames: whether two layers (indices 0-31 or names) collide. Every pair collides by default; bodies and character controllers collide only when their layers do. |
| `layerCollisions[].collide` | boolean | yes |   | Whether they collide. |
| `layerCollisions[].layers` | array of integer or string | yes |   | The two layers (the same twice: a layer with itself). Items: at least 2, at most 2. |
| `layerNames` | object | no |   | Names of collision layers by index (&quot;0&quot; to &quot;31&quot;), e.g. {&quot;1&quot;: &quot;Player&quot;, &quot;2&quot;: &quot;Debris&quot;}; &quot;&quot; or null clears a name. Names are unique (ignoring case), at most 64 characters, and RigidBody.Layer, CharacterController.Layer, scripts' Physics:\:GetLayerIndex and layerCollisions accept them. |
| `resetLayerCollisions` | boolean | no |   | Lets every pair of layers collide again before layerCollisions applies. |

## project.setGameInfo

Sets the game's identity, which exported games show: title (the window's title, the log, dialogs; empty: the project's name), version (one to four whole numbers from 0 to 65535 separated by dots, e.g. &quot;1.2.0&quot;), company and copyright (optional), at most 128 characters of text each without line breaks, and icon: a texture of the project whose source is a PNG, JPEG, TGA or BMP image (at least 256 x 256 pixels, square or centered on transparent pixels), or null for none (the game shows what its platform gives it: on Windows, the runtime's strata mark). Fields left out keep their values. The project's name stays the game's name for its save and log directories, so a new title or company never moves players' saves. One undo step that leaves the scene saved; writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it); allowed while playing. An invalid field changes nothing. Returns game (title, version, company, copyright, icon).

| `title` | string | no |   | The game's title (empty: the project's name). |

## project.setSettings

Sets one project settings section (project.settings lists them with their schemas) to a value, or with reset: true back to its default, as one undo step that leaves the scene saved, and writes the project file in the background (project.save waits for it). The value replaces the section's whole value (a simple section's fields left out take their defaults) and is checked by the section first: an invalid one changes nothing and fails naming the first bad field. Allowed while playing: the running game reads the change at once and it stays after play.stop. Returns section, value (what applies now) and isDefault.

## project.settings

The project's settings: its own fields (project: name, startScene, loadingScene, alwaysInclude, game: the game's identity; set with project.setStartScene, project.setExportSettings and project.setGameInfo) and every project settings section the engine's modules and the game register (sections: id, title, category, description, version, schema: the JSON Schema of its value, value: what applies, isDefault: whether the project leaves it at its default, problem: why a stored value is refused, null when none), in registration order; unclaimed lists sections the file stores that no module of this editor claims (kept as stored). section narrows sections to one. Set one with project.setSettings.
